module_mood_contract: M0 prework — not on the mood arc (mood arc opens at M1: joyful creation). Prework is almost entirely SETUP/LAUNCH beat (repo pick, session open, tarball fetch, extract+install, arrival hand-off, optional pre-read), mood-exempt per check_strategy_tie_in §1. Step 5 (pick a trivial bug + confirm readiness) is the sole TEACHING beat — rehearses the push-back move that recurs across the training. Close hands off verbatim into M1's Connections question, priming joyful creation without pre-empting it.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Forcing functions live in prompts, not body prose.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The step-5 push-back move is enacted by the registry prompt `{{prompt:ae101-prework-one-at-a-time}}`, not scripted in body prose. The body's 'push back if it dumps all four criteria at once' names the situation and hands the recovery move to the fence, matching the sole load-bearing forcing function in this file. The 'ask it to install gh if it isn't there' line (What to bring) is a readiness aside in the same register as the surrounding tracker/worktree bullets, not a scripted teaching move needing a fence. Commit 3683596 added one more bolded body line in the same section — 'Four sizes off your backlog. Not four slices of one task.' — a clarifying constraint on what the artifact-list means, not a prescribed student reaction or count-script; §16's boundary-2 carve-out (light instructional aside, not load-bearing session machinery) covers it without a fence.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Body teaches the work; trainer manages the room outside text.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No group/pair/share cues anywhere in the file (individual setup throughout: pick a repo, open a session, fetch and extract a bundle, pick a bug). Every sentence is about the student's own artifact or next action.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Mood contract named; mood-floor applies to teaching beats only.

'Come to Module 1 without one and you'll be scrambling for one while the exercise is already fixing bugs. Your call.' (Bring to Module 1) — names the consequence, not a wrongdoing; 'Your call' keeps the frame descriptive rather than shaming. trace.phases[7].mood_note confirms the epistemic-not-punitive read.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Lead with discipline, not failure mode.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Section headers and body throughout are positive-frame ('What to bring', 'Pick THE repo', 'Pick a trivial bug and confirm M1 readiness') — no failure-word-led framing (e.g. no header naming a mistake or violation).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Strategy-fidelity — no front-run, module-to-module arc holds, Big Idea honored, mood doesn't resolve early.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Close hands off verbatim into M1's Connections opener — 'what's one trick you figured out with Claude Code that nobody taught you?' matches getting-going.md line 36 word for word. Prework surfaces a bug and confirms readiness but does not fix it, so M1's fix-tests-first teaching moment is not front-run. Content-strategy's own line ('Orientation is short, not a setup ramp... Prework has done Claude Code install + repo-choice + bug-surfacing') is honored directly. Mood stays at 'curious/ready' throughout (trace.close.mood_note) rather than resolving into M1's joy, so M1's teaching moment isn't stolen. Commit 3683596 (page-geometry locator fix) touched only the intro's M2 thinking-effort clause (dropped a forward pointer for a self-contained reason) and added one clarifying bolded line in What to bring — neither touches the M1 handoff line or front-runs any downstream module.
